exposure: Hysteroscopic resection of cesarean scar pregnancy (CSP)
outcome: Postoperative drainage of the uterine cavity
Time for β-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG) to return to normal levels
cohort: 71 women with exogenous cesarean scar pregnancy treated at a tertiary medical center
finding: Laparoscopic resection of exogenous CSP was associated with a shorter time for serum β-hCG to return to normal levels and less postoperative drainage of the uterine cavity compared to hysteroscopic resection.
